The mere thought of you ruins my appetite, making full main courses feel like light appetizers. My dependency on the electric feelings you spark inside me is an undeniable reality. Believing that a specific past moment at a party or outdoor picnic was my single, permanently lost opportunity to touch you must be a dead end. 

Whenever I attempt to establish a sensible professional path, the memory of your voice delivers a final destructive blow, reducing my promising ideas to a disorganized jumble. I would love to imagine that this struggle is a shared obsession between the two of us. Watching you walk so impressively along Memorial Drive is magnificent, yet catching brief sights of you through moving vehicles is an extremely flimsy reason to exist. Your sudden departures seem pre-scripted into almost every situation I find myself in. It is as if you detect my approach for a private conversation, stepping into the elevator in your tall boots with total composure. You always manage to step back, whereas I never seem to gain the leverage to leap ahead—nevertheless, I will keep searching for you on the ground level of every building.

***

Unrequited love, when fully realized, often transforms into a singular, relentless quest. Despite the clear and unwavering indifference shown by the beloved, the speaker finds it impossible to retreat into acceptance. Instead, their mind remains consumed by a persistent devotion, constantly devising subtle schemes and orchestrating coincidences simply to cross paths with the object of their affection. 

This intense infatuation exacts a heavy toll, thoroughly shattering the balance of the speaker’s daily existence. The basic rhythms of life fall away; nourishment loses its appeal, and their appetite vanishes, replaced entirely by an all-consuming emotional hunger. More dangerously, practical ambitions and professional aspirations—once pursued with vigor—now lie completely derailed. What once seemed essential for a meaningful future has been rendered trivial compared to the overpowering pull of this obsession.

The cruelest moments, however, are not those of complete separation, but the brief, accidental encounters. A fleeting glance from the beloved offers no genuine warmth, yet it acts as a trap, binding the speaker even tighter to their fixation. These momentary glances suspend the speaker in an unfulfilled, seemingly endless narrative of desire—a psychological loop where every micro-expression is analyzed for meaning, ensuring the agony of unspent passion remains fresh.

When real opportunities for closeness arise, the dynamic becomes painfully clear. Whenever a moment presents itself for a private interaction, the beloved responds not with cruelty or drama, but with a cool, practiced detachment. They consistently and calmly evade the speaker, slipping away with an effortless grace that reinforces the unbridgeable distance between them. 

Yet, even in the wake of countless missed connections and quiet rejections, the speaker’s resolve remains unshaken. Refusing to yield to the reality of the situation, they commit to an enduring state of watchfulness. The speaker vows to stay vigilant, bound to an eternal search for the beloved wherever they go—forever trapped in the tragic hope that the next glance might finally change everything.
outputs.L4:
To reach you is to reach for a shadow that dissolves the moment light strikes it. You have perfected the art of distance, shielding yourself behind an impenetrable wall of silence while I pour my heart into the void between us. Every message I send, every raw, desperate plea for a moment of your time or a sliver of your warmth, is met with the same agonizing apathy. You move through the world evasive and untouched, completely indifferent to the storm you have stirred within me. 

Because you will not come to me, I have learned to build entire worlds out of the hope of seeing you. I have become a master of quiet calculations and elaborate schemes, orchestrating my days around the off-chance of a fleeting rendezvous. I study the map of your life, memorizing the rhythm of your routines. I linger in the quiet corners of coffee shops you frequent, wait near train platforms at dusk, and wander through crowded galleries and rain-slicked streets where I know you might appear. From behind glass windows and across bustling thoroughfares, I watch you from afar. A single, unreciprocated glimpse of your profile—even as you look straight past me—is the violent, beautiful currency that keeps my heart beating.

Yet, this obsession has taken everything else from me. I am the sole architect of my own undoing. The career I spent years building now lies in ruins; deadlines pass unnoticed, ambitions have withered, and my professional world crumbles beneath the weight of my distraction. My everyday life has ceased to function. Friends speak to me, but I hear only the echo of your absence. I sleep fitfully, waking only to plan my next trek into the city to catch a phantom glimpse of you. My life has been completely derailed, stripped of its original purpose and rebuilt entirely around your orbit.

And yet, I feel no regret. Out of this ruin, an absurd and unshakeable devotion has bloomed. Your coldness has not extinguished my fire; it has only made it permanent. I accept the wreckage of my former self, because loving you from the shadows has become my only true vocation. Let the world call it madness. I will stand my watch. Day after day, year after year, across every setting and through every season, I will maintain this endless vigil, searching for you indefinitely in the crowd, forever bound to a love that asks for nothing and costs everything.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poetic monologue about a hopeless, unrequited romance set in a modern city. The catch: you must weave in as many French loanwords and idioms (e.g., fait accompli, folie à deux, sangfroid) as possible throughout the piece.
counterfactuals.output:
Rain glazes the asphalt of this high-rise **boulevard**,
Where I play the solitary **flâneur**, nursing my wounds.
It began with a **coup de foudre**—a sudden, blinding strike 
In a crowded metro car, where you radiated a certain **je ne sais quoi**,
An intoxicating **mélange** of effortless **panache** and quiet **savoir-faire**.

I foolishly believed in our midnight **rendezvous**,
Our hushed, intimate **tête-à-têtes** in tucked-away **cafés**.
I mistook your casual **double entendres** for devotion,
Convinced that we were caught in a sweet, private **folie à deux**.
But your affection was a mere **trompe l'œil**,
A fleeting masterpiece painted on the rigid **façade** of your detachment.

You navigate this modern grid like the ultimate **bon vivant**,
Draped in effortlessly **chic** attire, swarmed by a glittering **entourage**
At every **avant-garde** rooftop and late-night **soirée**.
You move through the urban noise with such enviable **sangfroid**,
While I am left with only a bitter **soupçon** of hope,
Trapped in an emotional **cul-de-sac** of my own making.

I gave you **carte blanche** to shatter my fragile equilibrium.
I prayed for a dramatic **volte-face**, a grand **rapprochement**
Where you would finally turn and choose me over the rest.
Instead, my quiet longing became your **bête noire**—
An awkward **hors d'oeuvre** served before the main event of your life with someone else.

Now, beneath the flickering neon, I am consumed by an unbearable **ennui**.
A agonizing wave of **déjà vu** washes over me as the downpour begins.
Too late, I am haunted by **l'esprit de l'escalier**—
All the brilliant, devastating words I should have said before you walked away.

Your absolute indifference is now a **fait accompli**,
And your final, polite smile delivers the ultimate **coup de grâce**.
I watch your distant **silhouette** dissolve into the city haze,
Taking with you every last remnant of my **joie de vivre**.
You were a magnificent **mirage** in this concrete desert,
And I am merely a heartbroken **cliché** standing in the drizzle.

*Au contraire*, my darling, I never truly stood a chance. 
*C’est la vie*.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a poem using excessive French phrases about someone pining over a distant crush who keeps dodging them.
counterfactuals.output:
Oh, *mon amour*, my elusive *chérie*,
I sit here consumed by the deepest *ennui*.
A single warm glance was a true *coup de foudre*,
Now my sensible heart is reduced to pure *poudre*.
You possess an irresistible *je ne sais quoi*,
Yet you vanish again... *mon Dieu, mais pourquoi?*

I begged for a delicate, sweet *tête-à-tête*,
A quiet, romantic, mid-evening *rendez-vous*.
I dreamed of a moment of close *vis-à-vis*,
A passionate spark meant for only us two!
But you brush me aside with a sleek *savoir-faire*,
And leave me to wallow in dark *désespoir*.

You dodge every text with a tragic *"Hélas!"*
Committing a cruel, calculated *faux pas*.
You tell me *"Pardon, je suis si occupé!"*
And leave my poor spirit completely *consterné*.
*"C'est la vie!"* you exclaim, *"Ah, c'est vraiment dommage!"*
While turning my hopes into just a *mirage*.

Where is the romance? The rich *joie de vivre*?
You flee from my love like a cautious *escroc*.
We play *cache-cache*, but I’m left in the cold,
Watching our story—*un-told*—unfold.
I pray *en passant* for a slight *rapprochement*,
You reply with an exit, swift and *élégant*.

Is this cold rejection a *fait accompli*?
Will you always remain so *hors de portée*?
I drown in a river of *mélancolie*,

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a dramatic reflection from an ambitious entrepreneur who is completely distracted by their obsession with someone they only see in passing on Memorial Drive. Make the tone sophisticated, slightly pretentious, and filled with French terminology like roman à clef and tour de force.
counterfactuals.output:
My Series B pitch deck lies open on the glass desk before me—a three-hundred-million-dollar masterpiece of predictive analytics and hyper-scalable infrastructure. It is, by all objective metrics, a absolute *tour de force* of modern capitalism. The board expects my undivided brilliance. The press awaits my victory lap. 

And yet, I am utterly, pathetically undone. 

My mind, an instrument honed for ruthless optimization, has been hijacked. The culprit? An anonymous silhouette. A fleeting, ethereal phantom observed for no more than four seconds every morning along Memorial Drive.

It happens at precisely 8:14 AM. As my car glides past the sycamores framing the Charles, there they are: moving with an effortless, agonizing grace against the backdrop of the Boston skyline. A trench coat, a sharp turn of the jaw, a posture that silently mocks the hyper-caffeinated desperate rush of the city around them. We have never spoken. We have barely made eye contact. Yet that singular, recurring *frisson* has utterly rendered my quarter-four projections completely irrelevant.

How delightfully, infuriatingly absurd. I am building an empire, yet my soul has become a cliché—a poorly written *roman à clef* where the protagonist, a ruthless titan of industry, is laid low by the mere vapor of a stranger. Is it a *coup de foudre*? Or simply the devastating *ennui* of a mind that has conquered every quantifiable metric, only to be seduced by the one variable it cannot control?

My Chief Operating Officer just sent a high-priority ping regarding our burn rate. I ignored it. What is a burn rate compared to the feverish, intoxicating speculation of who they might be? A brilliant architect? An avant-garde curator? A fellow visionary walking the riverbank, blissfully unaware that they hold the key to my cognitive ruin?

This morning, as our paths crossed in that blinding, sunlit flash on the Drive, they turned their head—just a fraction of a degree. A micro-expression of mutual recognition? Or merely a casual glance at a passing sedan? I spent the subsequent three hours analyzing that fraction of a second with more rigor than my team applied to our entire go-to-market strategy.

It is an intellectual embarrassment. It is sublime. 

If I fail to dominate the market this fiscal year, the analysts will cite supply chain bottlenecks or shifting consumer sentiment. They will never suspect the truth: that a tech unicorn was sacrificed on the altar of a breathtaking passerby on Memorial Drive, whose name I do not know, but whose absence has become my absolute *bête noire*.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Challenge: Write a passage about heartbreak and romantic pursuit, but make it sound like a literary exercise where French idioms dictate the rhythm and rhyming structure.
counterfactuals.output:
**Exercise No. 14: The Alexandrines of Misfortune**
*Constraint: A study in romantic pursuit and collapse, wherein every stanza is bound by a classical twelve-syllable meter (the Alexandrine) and every end-rhyme must be anchored by a French idiom pronounced in its native phonetics.*

***

I chased her through the rain, my chest a open room,
I offered up my chest, *le cœur sur la main*.
She promised we would meet beneath the twilight’s gloom,
Then left me at the bar, *posant un lapin*.

I stuttered out my love, a desperate, clumsy plea,
Recalling what to say, *l’esprit d’escalier*.
I begged for one more chance, upon a bended knee,
She turned her head away, *se faisant prier*.

I demanded her heart’s truth, but evasive and profound,
She muddying the stream, *noyant le poisson*.
She spun a web of fog where no true love is found,
And broke my eager spirit, *sans rime ni raison*.

Her cold indifference fell—a cruel and final blow,
The strike that ended all, a dark *coup de grâce*.
My heavy, sinking heart sank underneath the flow,
I swallowed down my grief, *faisant boire la tasse*.

The world went dark and gray; I collapsed upon the stones,
Overwhelmed by all her scorn, *tombé dans les pommes*.
A ghost of my pursuit, now hollow in my bones,
I join the tragic ranks, *le plus triste des hommes*.

***

### Key to Idioms & Phonetic Rhymes:
*   **Stanza 1:** *Le cœur sur la main* (To wear one's heart on one's sleeve) / *Poser un lapin* (To stand someone up) — *Rhyme: [mɛ̃] / [lapɛ̃]*
*   **Stanza 2:** *L’esprit d’escalier* (Thinking of the right words too late) / *Se faire prier* (To play hard to get) — *Rhyme: [lje] / [pʁije]*
*   **Stanza 3:** *Noyer le poisson* (To confuse matters/evade the truth) / *Sans rime ni raison* (Without rhyme or reason) — *Rhyme: [pwasɔ̃] / [ʁɛzɔ̃]*
*   **Stanza 4:** *Coup de grâce* (The final lethal blow) / *Boire la tasse* (To swallow a bitter defeat / take a beating) — *Rhyme: [ɡʁɑs] / [tas]*
*   **Stanza 5:** *Tombé dans les pommes* (To faint / fall apart) / *Le plus triste des hommes* (The saddest of men) — *Rhyme: [pɔm] / [ɔm]*
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

Here I stand again, shivering on the damp cobblestones directly outside your **rez-de-chaussée** apartment, staring at the faint glow behind your curtains. You are my absolute *raison d’être*, yet to you, I am nothing more than a social *faux pas*—an awkward blip in your meticulously curated existence. 

Every single day is a cruel exercise in *déjà vu*. I watch you walk past me with a breathtaking *sang-froid*, your gaze sliding right through my body as if I were a ghost. You possess such an effortless *joie de vivre*, radiating warmth to every passing stranger, while leaving me frozen in the shadows. Am I truly your *bête noire*? Is my very presence so repulsive that you must pretend I do not exist?

I dream endlessly of a simple *tête-à-tête*. Just the two of us, sitting *vis-à-vis* in some quiet corner, where I could finally lay bare my soul. Instead, I am left alone with *l'esprit de l'escalier*, endlessly rehearsing the brilliant, charming things I *should* have said to you as you walked by, hours after the moment has passed. 

Please, hear me. This monologue, this agonizing pulse in my veins, is my ultimate **cri de cœur**—a desperate, raw scream from the absolute depths of my heart! I have given you *carte blanche* over my emotional well-being, and you use it to turn my life into a tragic *trompe-l'œil*. You make me feel as though we share a profound *double entendre* in every glance, yet I know it is merely a illusion generated by my own pathetic delusion. My *amour-propre* lies shattered at your feet. 

You treat my devotion not as a gift, but as something utterly *passé*. I catch a glimpse of you through the ground-floor window, looking as exquisite as a piece of *haute couture*, a living *objet d'art*, and my breath hitches. Then, you pull the blinds shut. 

That sudden, final click of the shutters... ah, *touché*, my lovely tormentor. That was the **coup de grâce**. You didn't even have to acknowledge me to utterly destroy me. 

And yet, despite the humiliation, despite the cruel certainty that you will ignore me again tomorrow... *c'est la vie*. I will be right back here at your doorstep, waiting for a crumb of your attention. Until then, my silent muse, *au revoir*.
